title: HVO-ARBiH Fighting Erupts at Gornji Vakuf
narrative: Heavy fighting breaks out between HVO and ARBiH forces in Gornji Vakuf as the HVO attempts to establish control over the town in line with the proposed Vance-Owen provincial boundaries. The clashes — involving tanks, artillery, and infantry — mark a significant escalation beyond the sporadic incidents of late 1992.

effects.text: HVO and ARBiH forces fight a pitched battle at Gornji Vakuf. The Vance-Owen provincial map becomes a pretext for Croat territorial grabs.

response_options.label: Respond with force
response_options.description: Send reinforcements to Gornji Vakuf. Escalates the confrontation significantly.

response_options.label: Seek a local ceasefire
response_options.description: Attempt to contain the fighting. De-escalates but does not resolve underlying tensions.

RBiH.headline: HVO reinforces Gornji Vakuf fight
RBiH.body: Herceg-Bosna sends reinforcements into the Gornji Vakuf clashes. Sarajevo staff see a significant escalation in the HVO-ARBiH confrontation and a sharper break in local cooperation.

RS.headline: HVO and ARBiH fighting intensifies
RS.body: Herceg-Bosna answers the Gornji Vakuf clashes with force. Pale analysts see the Vance-Owen provincial map becoming a pretext for deeper Croat-Bosniak fighting.

RBiH.headline: HVO seeks a local Gornji Vakuf ceasefire
RBiH.body: Herceg-Bosna tries to contain the fighting around Gornji Vakuf. Sarajevo sees de-escalation on the local front, though the underlying territorial dispute remains unresolved.

RS.headline: Gornji Vakuf fighting is contained for now
RS.body: Herceg-Bosna moves toward a local ceasefire rather than a wider escalation. Pale reads the alliance strain as real, but not yet a full rupture.

title: Western Powers Press Sarajevo: Engage with Vance-Owen
narrative: Western capitals make clear that continued international support depends on Sarajevo engaging seriously with the Vance-Owen Peace Plan. Lord Owen warns that Bosnian refusal risks isolating the government internationally.

effect.text: Western capitals press Sarajevo to engage seriously with the Vance-Owen Peace Plan or risk international isolation.

HRHB.headline: Sarajevo engages Vance-Owen pressure
HRHB.body: RBiH acknowledges Western pressure to engage seriously with the Vance-Owen Peace Plan. HVO staff see a more cooperative diplomatic posture, even as Sarajevo absorbs internal strain.

RS.headline: Sarajevo answers Western pressure
RS.body: RBiH signals that it will engage with the Vance-Owen process to preserve international support. Pale sees Sarajevo trading some leverage for patron confidence.

HRHB.headline: Sarajevo holds its Vance-Owen line
HRHB.body: RBiH maintains its position despite Western warnings about isolation. HVO staff see Sarajevo preserving negotiating leverage while risking patron confidence.

RS.headline: Sarajevo resists mediator pressure
RS.body: RBiH refuses to soften its Vance-Owen stance under Western pressure. Pale reads the move as a bid for leverage, with a visible cost to Sarajevo's international support.

title: Vance-Owen Peace Plan Presented
narrative: The Vance-Owen Peace Plan proposes dividing Bosnia into ten semi-autonomous provinces based on ethnic and geographic criteria. The plan is endorsed by the Bosnian Croats and reluctantly by the Bosniaks, but the Bosnian Serb assembly in Pale rejects it, dooming the most comprehensive peace effort to date.

effect.text: The Vance-Owen Plan is presented. All parties must decide whether to accept a negotiated partition of Bosnia.

response_options.label: Accept the Vance-Owen Plan
response_options.description: Accepting improves international credibility and may bring relief, but legitimizes territorial losses.

response_options.label: Reject the Vance-Owen Plan
response_options.description: Rejection preserves territorial claims but damages standing with the international community.

HRHB.headline: Sarajevo accepts Vance-Owen terms
HRHB.body: RBiH accepts the Vance-Owen Plan, improving international credibility while accepting a framework that legitimizes territorial losses. HVO leaders see Sarajevo moving into the same diplomatic channel.

RS.headline: Sarajevo accepts Vance-Owen
RS.body: RBiH accepts the Vance-Owen framework and gains international credibility. Pale sees Sarajevo accepting the partition formula while pressure shifts toward the Bosnian Serb assembly.

HRHB.headline: Sarajevo rejects Vance-Owen
HRHB.body: RBiH rejects the Vance-Owen Plan to preserve territorial claims. HVO leaders see Sarajevo keeping freedom of action at the cost of international standing.

RS.headline: Sarajevo refuses Vance-Owen
RS.body: RBiH rejects the proposed ten-province settlement and preserves its territorial claims. Pale sees Sarajevo taking a morale gain while damaging its international standing.

title: Kravica Raid on Orthodox Christmas
narrative: ARBiH forces under Naser Oric launch a raid from the Srebrenica enclave on the Serb village of Kravica on Orthodox Christmas Day, killing between 30-35 VRS soldiers and 11-13 Serb civilians. The attack provides the VRS a pretext for intensifying its spring offensive against the eastern enclaves. Oric is later indicted by the ICTY for failing to prevent crimes in the enclave's defense.

effects.text: The Christmas raid on Kravica galvanizes VRS commanders. The Drina Corps begins preparations for an offensive to crush the eastern enclaves once and for all.

historical_source: ICTY Oric Indictment (IT-03-68). Krstic Trial Judgment (IT-98-33-T), paras. 17-18.

title: Deputy Prime Minister Turajlic Assassinated
narrative: VRS soldiers stop a UN convoy transporting Bosnian Deputy Prime Minister Hakija Turajlic from Sarajevo Airport. After a 90-minute standoff, a Serb soldier shoots Turajlic seven times through the open door of a French UNPROFOR APC, killing him in front of five peacekeepers. He is the highest-ranking Bosnian official killed in the war.

effects.text: The murder of Turajlic inside a UN vehicle exposes the fragility of UNPROFOR's protection and the VRS's contempt for international norms.

historical_source: ICTY Karadzic Trial Judgment (IT-95-5/18-T), para. 5778.

title: Croat-Bosniak War Erupts
narrative: Full-scale fighting erupts between the HVO and the ARBiH across central Bosnia and Herzegovina. Emboldened by the Vance-Owen provincial map and Croatian political pressure, HVO forces launch coordinated offensives to secure territories claimed for Herceg-Bosna. What began as sporadic clashes at Prozor and Gornji Vakuf escalates into systematic ethnic cleansing on both sides, opening a devastating second front for the Bosnian government.

effects.text: The Croat-Bosniak alliance collapses. HVO and ARBiH forces engage in open warfare across central Bosnia.

title: Ahmici Massacre
narrative: HVO forces, supported by the Jokers special police unit, launch a coordinated attack on the Bosniak village of Ahmici in the Lasva Valley. Over 100 civilians are killed, including women and children, and the village is systematically burned. The massacre becomes one of the most documented war crimes of the conflict and a defining atrocity of the Croat-Bosniak war.

effects.text: The Ahmici massacre shocks the international community. HVO credibility suffers a devastating blow.

title: US Special Envoy — American Engagement Begins
narrative: President Clinton names Ambassador Reginald Bartholomew as the first US special envoy to Bosnia negotiations, signaling increased American engagement with the conflict. In May, Secretary of State Warren Christopher proposes a 'lift and strike' policy — lifting the arms embargo and using air strikes against VRS positions — but Britain and France reject it. Despite this setback, American diplomatic involvement has begun in earnest.

effects.text: American diplomacy enters the Bosnian arena. The 'lift and strike' proposal fails in Europe, but Washington's trajectory toward intervention has begun.

historical_source: US State Department, 'Bosnia: Road to the Dayton Peace Agreement.'

title: VRS Cerska-Konjevic Polje Offensive
narrative: The VRS Drina Corps, supported by Yugoslav Army armor, launches Operation Cerska, overrunning Bosniak-held positions at Cerska and Konjevic Polje in eastern Bosnia. The offensive severs the land link between the Srebrenica and Zepa enclaves, reducing the Srebrenica pocket to 150 square kilometers and driving 50,000-60,000 refugees into the overcrowded town.

effects.text: Cerska and Konjevic Polje fall to the Drina Corps. Srebrenica is now completely isolated and bursting with refugees.

historical_source: ICTY Krstic Trial Judgment (IT-98-33-T), paras. 15-22. Mladic Trial Judgment (IT-09-92-T).

title: HVO Besieges East Mostar
narrative: HVO forces impose a complete blockade on the eastern bank of Mostar, cutting off the Bosniak population from food, water, and medical supplies. Systematic shelling targets the densely populated old town. An estimated 55,000 Bosniaks are trapped in increasingly desperate conditions as the HVO seeks to drive them from the city entirely.

effects.text: East Mostar is besieged. 55,000 Bosniaks are trapped as HVO forces impose a total blockade on the eastern bank.

title: UN Resolution 808 — International Tribunal Announced
narrative: The UN Security Council passes Resolution 808, deciding that an international tribunal shall be established for the prosecution of serious violations of international humanitarian law in the former Yugoslavia. The resolution signals growing judicial attention to wartime atrocities and serves as the direct precursor to the ICTY's formal establishment in May.

effects.text: Resolution 808 puts all commanders on notice: the international community is documenting crimes and building the architecture for prosecution.

historical_source: UN Security Council Resolution 808 (1993), S/RES/808.

title: Central Bosnia Engulfed in Three-Way War
narrative: Central Bosnia becomes a patchwork of overlapping front lines as VRS, HVO, and ARBiH forces fight simultaneously. Towns like Travnik, Vitez, and Busovaca change hands or are divided street by street. The three-way nature of the conflict creates impossible tactical situations and widespread civilian suffering.

effect.text: Three-way fighting engulfs central Bosnia. The overlapping front lines create a humanitarian catastrophe.

title: Zagreb Restrains Boban: Hold Back During VOPP Window
narrative: Tuđman quietly orders Boban to restrain HVO offensive operations. The Vance-Owen provincial map is favorable to Croat Herzegovina — Zagreb needs HRHB to accept the plan, not derail it through military escalation.

effect.text: Zagreb quietly orders Boban to hold back HVO offensive operations during the Vance-Owen window.

title: General Morillon Enters Srebrenica
narrative: UNPROFOR Commander General Philippe Morillon reaches the besieged Srebrenica enclave after months of convoy blockades. Confronted by desperate civilians, he publicly declares 'You are now under the protection of the United Nations. I will never abandon you.' His personal guarantee raises hopes but lacks any enforcement mechanism.

effects.text: Morillon's dramatic declaration creates an obligation the UN cannot fulfill. The gap between his promise and UNPROFOR's means defines the enclave's tragic position.

historical_source: ICTY Krstic Trial Judgment (IT-98-33-T), para. 20. MSF Speaking Out: Srebrenica 1993-2003.

title: Srebrenica Under Heavy Bombardment
narrative: The VRS intensifies its assault on the Srebrenica enclave, systematically shelling the overcrowded town. Thousands of refugees huddle in schools and public buildings as artillery rounds fall indiscriminately. General Morillon's dramatic personal guarantee becomes a symbol of the UN's agonizing position.

effects.text: Srebrenica is bombarded relentlessly. International outcry mounts as the enclave's humanitarian situation deteriorates.

title: UN Resolution 816 — No-Fly Zone Enforcement
narrative: The UN Security Council passes Resolution 816, authorizing member states to enforce the no-fly zone over Bosnia-Herzegovina that had been violated over 500 times since its establishment in October 1992. On April 12 NATO commences Operation Deny Flight with combat air patrols, marking a shift from passive monitoring to active military involvement.

effects.text: NATO combat aircraft now patrol Bosnian airspace. The VRS loses its fixed-wing air support but retains overwhelming ground-based fire superiority.

historical_source: UN Security Council Resolution 816 (1993), S/RES/816. Operation Deny Flight USAF history.

title: Croatia Tightens Control over Herceg-Bosna
narrative: The Republic of Croatia deepens its de facto control over the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna: HV officers serve in HVO command positions, Croatian state resources flow across the border, and Zagreb's directives increasingly drive HVO military strategy. The ICTY Prlic trial establishes a Joint Criminal Enterprise involving Tudjman's inner circle and HVO commanders aimed at creating ethnically homogeneous Croat territory for eventual annexation.

effects.text: Zagreb's patronage deepens. HVO commanders receive Croatian Army support — and with it, the expectation that Herceg-Bosna will serve Croatian strategic interests.

historical_source: ICTY Prlic Trial Judgment (IT-04-74-T), JCE findings. ICTY Appeals Judgment (IT-04-74-A).

title: Sovici-Doljani Attack
narrative: HVO forces attack the Bosniak villages of Sovici and Doljani near Jablanica, detaining approximately 400 Bosniak civilians and capturing 70-75 ARBiH soldiers. The attack occurs simultaneously with the Ahmici massacre in the Lasva Valley, revealing coordinated HVO operations across both central Bosnia and Herzegovina.

effects.text: Coordinated HVO operations strike from Jablanica to the Lasva Valley simultaneously. The scale reveals systematic planning behind what the HVO publicly frames as defensive action.

historical_source: ICTY Prlic Trial Judgment (IT-04-74-T), Vol. 2. ICTY Naletilic-Martinovic Trial Judgment (IT-98-34-T).

title: Trusina Killings
narrative: ARBiH forces kill 15 Croat civilians and 7 HVO prisoners of war in the village of Trusina near Konjic, on the same day as the Ahmici massacre. The reciprocal atrocities illustrate the descending cycle of ethnic violence that the Croat-Bosniak war has unleashed across central Bosnia.

effects.text: War crimes on both sides deepen mutual hatred. Each atrocity becomes justification for the next.

historical_source: Court of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Case S1 1 K 017327 16 Kre2.

title: UN Resolution 819 — Srebrenica Safe Area
narrative: The UN Security Council passes Resolution 819, declaring Srebrenica a 'safe area' free from armed attack or any hostile act, and demanding an immediate VRS ceasefire and unimpeded humanitarian access. The declaration creates a promise of protection without committing the military means to enforce it.

effects.text: Srebrenica is declared a UN safe area. The VRS ignores the ceasefire demand while the UN lacks any credible enforcement mechanism.

historical_source: UN Security Council Resolution 819 (1993), S/RES/819.

title: UN Resolution 820 — Tightened Sanctions on Serbia
narrative: The Security Council passes Resolution 820, substantially reinforcing the sanctions regime against Serbia and Montenegro. Following the Bosnian Serb assembly's rejection of the Vance-Owen plan on April 26, all commodity transport across Serbian borders is prohibited except medical supplies and foodstuffs, further strangling the RS supply chain through its patron.

effects.text: The tightened embargo enters force. Belgrade's ability to sustain the VRS is visibly constrained, and Milosevic's patience with Pale is running thin.

historical_source: UN Security Council Resolution 820 (1993), S/RES/820.

title: Srebrenica Demilitarization Agreement
narrative: Under intense international pressure following the VRS assault on Srebrenica, Generals Mladic and Halilovic sign a demilitarization agreement on April 17-18: the ARBiH is to surrender weapons under UNPROFOR supervision in exchange for a ceasefire and UN troop deployment. Implementation is flawed on both sides — the ARBiH hides weapons while the VRS continues to restrict humanitarian convoys.

effect.text: The demilitarization agreement is signed. Srebrenica is technically disarmed — but both sides are already maneuvering around its terms.

response_options.label: Comply fully with disarmament
response_options.description: Surrender all weapons as demanded. Gains international credibility but leaves the enclave defenseless.

response_options.label: Comply in appearance, hide weapons
response_options.description: Surrender visible stocks while concealing reserves. The historical choice — preserving minimum defense capability.

response_options.label: Refuse disarmament
response_options.description: Publicly reject the agreement. Maintains military capability but draws international condemnation and increased VRS pressure.

RS.headline: RBiH accepts Srebrenica disarmament
RS.body: RBiH commanders accept full weapons surrender under UNPROFOR supervision. Pale sees Sarajevo gaining mediator credibility while the enclave's defense becomes more exposed.

HRHB.headline: RBiH accepts Srebrenica disarmament
HRHB.body: RBiH commanders accept full weapons surrender under UNPROFOR supervision. Mostar sees Sarajevo trading enclave military capacity for stronger standing with international mediators.

RS.headline: RBiH hedges Srebrenica disarmament
RS.body: RBiH commanders surrender visible stocks while preserving hidden reserves. Pale sees formal compliance language paired with an effort to keep minimum defense capability inside the enclave.

HRHB.headline: RBiH hedges Srebrenica disarmament
HRHB.body: RBiH commanders surrender visible stocks while preserving hidden reserves. Mostar sees Sarajevo trying to satisfy UNPROFOR supervision without leaving the enclave fully exposed.

RS.headline: RBiH rejects Srebrenica disarmament
RS.body: RBiH commanders reject the demilitarization terms and keep the enclave armed. Pale sees preserved military capability at the cost of international condemnation and renewed pressure.

HRHB.headline: RBiH rejects Srebrenica disarmament
HRHB.body: RBiH commanders reject the demilitarization terms and keep the enclave armed. Mostar sees Sarajevo accepting diplomatic damage to avoid surrendering the enclave's remaining defense.

historical_source: ICTY Krstic Trial Judgment (IT-98-33-T), paras. 23-27. Halilovic-Mladic Agreement, May 8 1993.

title: UN Declares Safe Areas
narrative: The UN Security Council passes Resolution 819, declaring Srebrenica a safe area, followed by Resolution 824 extending protection to Sarajevo, Tuzla, Zepa, Gorazde, and Bihac. The resolutions promise protection without committing adequate military force to deliver it — a fatal gap between mandate and means that will have catastrophic consequences.

effects.text: Six UN safe areas are declared. The promise of protection raises hope among besieged populations, but no credible enforcement mechanism exists.

title: Milošević Orders Karadžić: Accept Vance-Owen
narrative: Milošević and Bulatović fly to Zvornik to personally demand that the Bosnian Serb Assembly accept the Vance-Owen Plan. Belgrade cannot sustain UN sanctions indefinitely — Pale's intransigence is destroying Serbia's economy.

effect.text: Milošević and Bulatović personally demand that the Bosnian Serb Assembly accept the Vance-Owen Plan.

title: Vitez-Kiseljak Pockets Isolated
narrative: As the Croat-Bosniak war intensifies, HVO garrisons in the Vitez-Busovaca pocket and the Kiseljak enclave become increasingly cut off from resupply by HVO main forces in western Herzegovina. The pockets must survive on local resources and intermittent VRS cooperation, while the ARBiH weighs the cost of an assault against the benefits of encirclement.

effects.text: HVO defenders in central Bosnia fight with the desperation of encirclement. Each convoy that fails to reach them deepens the crisis.

historical_source: ICTY Kordic Trial Judgment (IT-95-14/2-T). ICTY Blaskic Trial Judgment (IT-95-14-T).

title: Bosnian Serb Assembly Rejects Vance-Owen Plan
narrative: Despite Karadzic's personal signature on the Vance-Owen plan on April 30, the Republika Srpska National Assembly in Pale votes to reject it on May 5-6, referring the decision to a referendum. The subsequent referendum produces a 96% rejection. Lord Owen declares the plan dead on June 18 — the last comprehensive peace proposal that preserved a unified Bosnia has failed.

effect.text: The Assembly has spoken. The Vance-Owen plan is dead. The war continues on Pale's terms.

response_options.label: Accept the assembly's vote
response_options.description: The people have spoken. Reject international pressure and continue the war. Internal cohesion is preserved but Serbia is furious.

response_options.label: Attempt to override the assembly
response_options.description: Defy the nationalist vote and push for acceptance. Historically impossible — risks fracturing the RS political structure.

HRHB.headline: Pale accepts the assembly rejection
HRHB.body: Republika Srpska accepts the Pale assembly vote against Vance-Owen and continues the war. HVO leaders see RS internal cohesion preserved while Belgrade's anger and international isolation grow.

RBiH.headline: RS assembly rejection stands
RBiH.body: Republika Srpska accepts the assembly's rejection of Vance-Owen. Sarajevo sees the comprehensive peace proposal fail while Pale preserves cohesion and absorbs heavier outside pressure.

HRHB.headline: Pale tries to override its assembly
HRHB.body: Republika Srpska leadership attempts to push acceptance despite the assembly vote. HVO staff see improved diplomatic posture for Pale, but a serious fracture inside RS politics.

RBiH.headline: RS leadership challenges the assembly vote
RBiH.body: Republika Srpska tries to override the nationalist rejection of Vance-Owen. Sarajevo sees a possible diplomatic opening, paired with visible strain in Pale's political structure.

historical_source: ICTY Karadzic Trial Judgment (IT-95-5/18-T), paras. 3526-3530. RS National Assembly proceedings, May 5-6 1993.

title: ICTY Formally Established — Resolution 827
narrative: The UN Security Council unanimously passes Resolution 827, formally establishing the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia — the first war crimes court created by the UN since Nuremberg and Tokyo. The tribunal has jurisdiction over genocide, crimes against humanity, and violations of the laws of war committed in the former Yugoslavia since 1991. While indictments are years away, the era of impunity may be ending.

effects.text: The ICTY opens for business in The Hague. Every commander who orders atrocities now does so with knowledge that a court exists to try them.

historical_source: UN Security Council Resolution 827 (1993), S/RES/827.

title: Battle of Travnik — ARBiH Recaptures City
narrative: The ARBiH 3rd Corps launches an offensive against HVO positions in Travnik, overwhelming the garrison within days. Thousands of Croat civilians flee across VRS lines rather than remain under ARBiH control. The loss of Travnik is a major setback for the HVO in central Bosnia, demonstrating the ARBiH's growing numerical superiority in the interior.

effects.text: Travnik falls to the ARBiH. Croat civilians flee, and the HVO's position in central Bosnia begins its terminal decline.

historical_source: ICTY Hadzihasanovic Trial Judgment (IT-01-47-T).

title: Operation Neretva '93
narrative: The ARBiH launches Operation Neretva '93 against HVO positions in Herzegovina and the Neretva Valley. The offensive aims to break the HVO siege of East Mostar and secure a corridor to the coast. Fierce fighting erupts around Jablanica and along the Neretva River as the ARBiH attempts to exploit its growing numerical advantage.

effect.text: The ARBiH launches Operation Neretva '93, striking at HVO positions in the Neretva Valley and around Mostar.

title: UN Resolution 836 — Use of Force Authorized
narrative: The Security Council passes Resolution 836, authorizing UNPROFOR to use force in reply to bombardments against safe areas and permitting member states to use 'all necessary measures through the use of air power' in and around them. This is the legal foundation for future NATO air strikes — though the dual-key arrangement between the UN and NATO means the authorization exists largely on paper.

effects.text: NATO now has legal authority to strike VRS positions. Whether it has the political will to use it is another question entirely.

historical_source: UN Security Council Resolution 836 (1993), S/RES/836.

title: Operation Sharp Guard — NATO Naval Blockade
narrative: NATO and the Western European Union begin Operation Sharp Guard, a combined naval blockade in the Adriatic Sea to enforce UN sanctions against the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the arms embargo on all former Yugoslav republics. The operation intercepts merchant shipping, tightening the economic noose on Serbia while limiting — though not eliminating — arms flows to all parties.

effects.text: NATO warships enforce the Adriatic blockade. Serbia's supply corridor tightens further, but the arms embargo continues to hurt the outgunned ARBiH most.

historical_source: NATO Operation Sharp Guard records. UN Security Council sanctions monitoring reports.

title: HVO Detention Camps Established
narrative: Following the eruption of full-scale Croat-Bosniak war, HVO forces conduct mass arrests of Bosniak men across Herzegovina, including Bosniak members of the HVO itself. Thousands are held in a network of camps including Dretelj Prison, Gabela, and the Heliodrom complex near Mostar. Conditions are brutal — overcrowding, starvation, beatings, and forced labor — paralleling the Serb-run camps revealed at Omarska the previous year.

effects.text: Images of Bosniak men crowded behind Heliodrom wire reach the international press. Croatia's patron relationship with the West enters a period of severe strain.

historical_source: ICTY Prlic Trial Judgment (IT-04-74-T), Vol. 3. ICTY Naletilic-Martinovic Trial Judgment (IT-98-34-T).

title: Sarajevo Tunnel Completed
narrative: After four months of secret construction under the codename 'Objekt BD,' the 800-meter tunnel connecting besieged Dobrinja to free territory at Butmir — passing under the UN-controlled airport runway — is completed. The tunnel carries up to 20 tonnes of supplies daily: food, weapons, ammunition, and communications equipment. It transforms Sarajevo's siege from a total blockade into a strangled but survivable containment.

effects.text: Sarajevo breathes again. The tunnel is a military and psychological lifeline — proof that the city's will to resist can find a way through any encirclement.

historical_source: Sarajevo Tunnel Museum archives. ICTY Galic Trial Judgment (IT-98-29-T).

title: Operation Lukavac 93 — VRS Offensive on Igman
narrative: The VRS launches Operation Lukavac 93 with 15,000 troops against ARBiH positions on Mount Igman and Bjelasnica, aiming to sever Sarajevo's last supply route. VRS forces capture the Igman road on August 4, bringing the city to the brink of total isolation. The offensive provokes the first credible NATO threat of air strikes, forcing VRS withdrawal under a UN-brokered agreement by August 14.

effect.text: VRS forces have seized the Igman road. Sarajevo faces total isolation — and NATO is issuing its first genuine ultimatum.

response_options.label: Comply with withdrawal demand
response_options.description: Pull back from Igman under the UN-brokered agreement. Avoids NATO strikes but concedes the strategic gain.

response_options.label: Defy NATO — hold Igman
response_options.description: Call NATO's bluff and hold the captured positions. Risks triggering the first NATO combat strikes in history.

RBiH.headline: VRS withdraws from Igman under pressure
RBiH.body: RS accepts the UN-brokered withdrawal demand after the Lukavac 93 advance. Sarajevo sees the immediate threat to the Igman route ease, while VRS gives up a strategic gain.

HRHB.headline: VRS complies on Igman withdrawal
HRHB.body: RS pulls back from the Igman positions rather than trigger NATO strikes. Mostar sees Western pressure contain the offensive, with VRS credibility taking a cost.

RBiH.headline: VRS defies NATO over Igman
RBiH.body: RS holds the captured Igman positions despite the threat of air strikes. Sarajevo faces renewed isolation pressure, while the risk of NATO combat action rises sharply.

HRHB.headline: VRS holds Igman against NATO warning
HRHB.body: RS calls the air-strike threat and keeps the Igman gains. Mostar sees stronger VRS battlefield posture, but also a more dangerous confrontation with NATO.

historical_source: ICTY Mladic Trial Judgment (IT-09-92-T). Washington Post, Aug 14 1993.

title: Maglaj Enclave Under Joint HVO-VRS Blockade
narrative: Following the collapse of the ARBiH-HVO alliance, the HVO joins the VRS in imposing a complete blockade on the Bosniak-held pocket around Maglaj, trapping approximately 100,000 people. The town endures relentless bombardment and near-total isolation for nine months, surviving partly on US airdrop supplies. The joint siege exemplifies the impossible tactical situation the ARBiH now faces — encircled from two directions simultaneously.

effects.text: Maglaj's joint blockade is a new strategic reality: the ARBiH must now defend against coordinated Serb and Croat pressure in the same valley.

historical_source: ICTY Prlic Trial Judgment (IT-04-74-T).

title: Battle of Bugojno
narrative: The ARBiH 307th Brigade attacks HVO positions in Bugojno in central Bosnia, where the defending Eugen Kvaternik Brigade can muster only 200-400 effective troops. After ten days of street fighting the ARBiH secures control of the town and captures significant military equipment, including tanks and artillery, consolidating control over the Vrbas River valley.

effects.text: Bugojno falls and its HVO arsenal is absorbed into the ARBiH. The momentum in central Bosnia has decisively shifted.

historical_source: ICTY Hadzihasanovic Trial Judgment (IT-01-47-T).

title: Sarajevo Market Areas Under Fire
narrative: Repeated mortar and artillery strikes target civilian areas in Sarajevo, including crowded marketplaces. Each incident draws international condemnation and edges the international community closer to considering military intervention against VRS positions. The SRK maintains its bombardment despite cease-fire agreements.

effects.text: Artillery continues to target civilian areas in Sarajevo. International pressure for intervention builds steadily.

title: Belgrade Grows Distant: Milošević Signals Exhaustion
narrative: After the Owen-Stoltenberg plan collapses, Milošević signals through back-channels that Serbia's patience is exhausted. UN sanctions are cratering the Serbian economy — Pale's demands are no longer Belgrade's priority.

effect.text: Milošević signals through back-channels that Serbia's patience with Pale is exhausted.

title: NATO Threatens Air Strikes — Sarajevo Ultimatum
narrative: NATO formally agrees to launch air strikes against Bosnian Serb positions if the strangulation of Sarajevo or attacks on other safe areas continue. The decision marks the first time the Alliance has authorized potential force in its 44-year history. The dual-key arrangement between UN and NATO commands means execution remains politically constrained, but the threat forces the VRS withdrawal from Mount Igman.

effects.text: NATO's ultimatum is the clearest signal yet that the international community may use force. The VRS calculates its next move carefully.

historical_source: NATO Council decision, August 9 1993. Operation Deny Flight history.

title: Owen-Stoltenberg Plan Proposed
narrative: International mediators David Owen and Thorvald Stoltenberg present a new peace plan proposing a loose union of three ethnic republics. The plan effectively legitimizes ethnic partition and is seen by the Bosnian government as rewarding aggression. Negotiations continue through the autumn amid ongoing fighting on all fronts.

effect.text: The Owen-Stoltenberg Plan proposes a tripartite union of ethnic republics. Each faction must weigh the costs of acceptance or rejection.

response_options.label: Accept the Owen-Stoltenberg Framework
response_options.description: Accepting brings international relief but concedes the principle of a unified Bosnia.

response_options.label: Reject Ethnic Partition
response_options.description: Rejection defends sovereignty but prolongs the war and frustrates mediators.

HRHB.headline: Sarajevo accepts Owen-Stoltenberg
HRHB.body: RBiH accepts the Owen-Stoltenberg framework and gains international relief. HVO leaders see Sarajevo conceding the principle of a unified Bosnia under a tripartite republic formula.

RS.headline: Sarajevo accepts Owen-Stoltenberg
RS.body: RBiH accepts the proposed union of ethnic republics, improving diplomatic credibility while conceding the unity principle. Pale sees Sarajevo moving onto the mediator track.

HRHB.headline: Sarajevo rejects ethnic partition
HRHB.body: RBiH rejects the Owen-Stoltenberg framework as a partition formula. HVO leaders see Sarajevo defending sovereignty while prolonging the war and frustrating mediators.

RS.headline: Sarajevo refuses Owen-Stoltenberg
RS.body: RBiH rejects the tripartite republic framework and accepts the diplomatic cost. Pale sees Sarajevo preserve its sovereignty claim while mediator pressure rises.

title: Owen-Stoltenberg: Accept or Resist?
narrative: Owen and Stoltenberg present their Union of Three Republics plan. Intelligence suggests Karadzic will not accept the RS territorial allocation. Accepting may isolate RS diplomatically — at the cost of legitimizing partition.
historical_source: ICTY IT-95-5/18-T (Karadzic trial, Izetbegovic O-S initialing, August 1993). Owen, David. Balkan Odyssey (1995).

effect.text: The Owen-Stoltenberg plan reaches the Bosnian government. Izetbegovic must decide whether to accept — knowing RS will reject it — or refuse partition on principle.

HRHB.headline: Sarajevo tactically accepts the plan
HRHB.body: RBiH accepts the Union of Three Republics plan for diplomatic advantage, expecting RS rejection. HVO leaders see Sarajevo gain international standing while legitimizing partition in principle.

RS.headline: Sarajevo accepts for diplomatic leverage
RS.body: RBiH accepts the Owen-Stoltenberg plan while calculating that Pale will reject its territorial allocation. RS staff see Sarajevo trying to isolate them diplomatically.

HRHB.headline: Sarajevo rejects partition on principle
HRHB.body: RBiH refuses the Union of Three Republics plan and accepts the cost to international standing. HVO leaders see Sarajevo preserve its sovereignty claim and negotiating leverage.

RS.headline: Sarajevo rejects Owen-Stoltenberg
RS.body: RBiH refuses partition on principle instead of accepting for optics. Pale sees Sarajevo give up a diplomatic isolation play in order to preserve its core territorial claim.

title: Grabovica and Uzdol Massacres
narrative: During Operation Neretva 93, ARBiH units from Sarajevo commit war crimes against Croat civilians: at least 13 villagers killed at Grabovica on September 8-9, and at least 29 civilians and one HVO POW killed at Uzdol on September 14. ICTY Chief of Staff Sefer Halilovic is indicted but acquitted due to insufficient evidence of effective command control over the perpetrators.

effects.text: ARBiH atrocities in Herzegovina are documented. No faction in this war holds clean hands.

historical_source: ICTY Halilovic Trial Judgment (IT-01-48-T).

title: Fikret Abdic Declares Autonomous Province
narrative: Fikret Abdic, the powerful Bihac businessman who actually won more votes than Izetbegovic in the 1990 presidential election, declares the Autonomous Province of Western Bosnia centered on Velika Kladusa. His breakaway entity, backed by both the VRS and the Republic of Serbian Krajina, opens a new internal front that splits the Bihac pocket and diverts 5th Corps resources away from the external siege.

effects.text: Abdic declares the Autonomous Province of Western Bosnia. The Bihac pocket is now fighting a war within a war.

title: Bosnian Parliament Rejects Owen-Stoltenberg Plan
narrative: After sessions aboard HMS Invincible on September 20, the Bosnian government assembly in Sarajevo votes to reject the Owen-Stoltenberg plan's ethnic partition, demanding additional territory and access to the sea. The rejection prolongs the war and frustrates international mediators but preserves the principle of a unified, multi-ethnic Bosnia.

effects.text: The Bosnian assembly refuses partition. The war will continue — but so will Bosnia's legal claim to its full territory.

historical_source: Peace plans proposed before and during the Bosnian War. HMS Invincible negotiations, September 20 1993.

title: Abdic-Karadzic Pact
narrative: Fikret Abdic signs a declaration with RS President Radovan Karadzic recognizing the Autonomous Province of Western Bosnia's sovereignty. The VRS commits to non-aggression, joint defense coordination, and logistical support including arms supplies, while the RSK also provides backing. The pact transforms the Bihac pocket into a three-way battleground: 5th Corps against Abdic's APWB forces backed by both Serb entities.

effects.text: Abdic and Karadzic formalize their alliance. The 5th Corps now faces encirclement from three directions — VRS, RSK, and APWB.

historical_source: Abdic-Karadzic Declaration, Oct 22 1993. ICTY Karadzic Trial Judgment (IT-95-5/18-T).

title: Stupni Do Massacre
narrative: HVO special units 'Apostoli' and 'Maturice' under Ivica Rajic attack the Bosniak village of Stupni Do near Vares, killing approximately 31 civilians and destroying the village. Over 250 Bosniak men in nearby Vares are rounded up and subjected to inhuman treatment. When UNPROFOR attempts to investigate, HVO forces obstruct access for days before the evidence is documented.

effects.text: Stupni Do is added to the growing list of documented HVO atrocities. Rajic will eventually plead guilty at The Hague.

historical_source: ICTY Rajic Sentencing Judgment (IT-95-12-S).

title: Stari Most Destroyed in Mostar
narrative: HVO forces destroy the iconic Stari Most, the 16th-century Ottoman bridge spanning the Neretva River in Mostar. The deliberate demolition of this UNESCO-recognized cultural monument becomes a global symbol of the war's cultural devastation. The act draws widespread international condemnation and deepens the stigma on the Bosnian Croat war effort.

effects.text: The Stari Most is destroyed by HVO shelling. The loss of the iconic bridge becomes a symbol of cultural destruction.

title: Strategic Posture Review
narrative: The war enters another grinding phase. Your army holds — barely. The international community offers sympathy but not intervention. Your commanders request more men, more guns, more time. The corridors are strained, the enclaves are fragile, and the political situation in Sarajevo grows more tense with each week of siege. What is your posture for the months ahead?

effect.text: The presidency convenes to review the strategic situation.

response_options.label: Press the offensive
response_options.description: Demand forward momentum from your corps commanders. The army attacks wherever it can. Supply costs rise, but morale soars and international attention focuses on Bosniak military capability.

response_options.label: Consolidate and defend
response_options.description: Halt costly attacks. Dig in on current lines, restore cohesion, and build reserves. The army that survives the winter can fight in the spring.

response_options.label: Signal openness to negotiations
response_options.description: Engage the international community. Signal willingness to negotiate. International standing improves and patron pressure eases, but hardliners in your own government are furious.

response_options.label: Accept ceasefire terms to buy time
response_options.description: The war has ground your forces down. Accept international mediation and a temporary ceasefire. The army desperately needs to rest and rearm — but your hardliners will call it surrender.

HRHB.headline: Sarajevo orders a more aggressive posture
HRHB.body: RBiH commanders are directed to seek forward momentum wherever supply allows. HVO staff see higher Bosnian morale, but also heavier pressure on shared logistics and coordination.

RS.headline: Sarajevo signals offensive intent
RS.body: RBiH leadership pushes its corps commanders toward renewed attacks. Pale reads the posture as a morale play that may raise pressure along exposed fronts.

HRHB.headline: Sarajevo shifts to consolidation
HRHB.body: RBiH halts costly attacks to restore cohesion and build reserves. HVO planners see a more defensive Bosnian posture while the army prepares for later operations.

RS.headline: RBiH digs in on current lines
RS.body: Sarajevo orders its forces to defend, rebuild, and preserve supply. Pale expects fewer immediate attacks but stronger prepared positions over time.

HRHB.headline: Sarajevo opens a diplomatic posture
HRHB.body: RBiH signals willingness to engage mediators. HVO leaders see improved international standing for Sarajevo, alongside visible strain among Bosnian hardliners.

RS.headline: Sarajevo signals negotiation readiness
RS.body: RBiH turns toward international engagement to ease pressure and improve standing. Pale weighs whether the move creates leverage or simply buys Sarajevo time.

HRHB.headline: Sarajevo accepts a ceasefire pause
HRHB.body: RBiH accepts mediation terms to rest and rearm. HVO staff note the logistical benefit for Sarajevo, even as internal critics frame the pause as weakness.

RS.headline: RBiH accepts ceasefire terms
RS.body: Sarajevo chooses a temporary pause to recover supply and cohesion. Pale reads the lower aggression as useful, but not as a final settlement.

title: Strategic Posture Review
narrative: The international community grows increasingly hostile. Belgrade's patience with Pale is wearing thin. Your generals report that the lines are solid — but the sanctions bite deeper each month, and the VRS cannot sustain current operational tempo indefinitely. The question before you is not whether you can win, but what victory means in a war the world wants to end.

effect.text: The RS Assembly demands a presidential assessment of the strategic situation.

response_options.label: Press territorial gains
response_options.description: Push further. Consolidate the corridor, tighten the enclaves, expand the buffer zone. What the VRS holds today, the final map must recognize.

response_options.label: Consolidate what we hold
response_options.description: Stop the costly advance and fortify current positions. Dig in on the Posavina corridor, on the Drina, on the approaches to Sarajevo. Hold what our soldiers have won.

response_options.label: Negotiate from strength
response_options.description: Engage the international mediators from a position of military advantage. Belgrade's pressure becomes manageable if you demonstrate willingness to talk — while holding every kilometer.

response_options.label: Accept a partition framework
response_options.description: The war has cost more than our people can bear. Signal willingness to accept a territorial settlement in exchange for international recognition. The hardliners in the Assembly will revolt — but the alternative is permanent isolation.

HRHB.headline: Pale orders continued territorial pressure
HRHB.body: RS leadership pushes for further gains and consolidation of key corridors. HVO staff expect higher VRS tempo and greater pressure on contested lines.

RBiH.headline: RS presses for more territory
RBiH.body: Pale signals that current holdings are not enough for the final map. Sarajevo reads the posture as a renewed push against corridors, enclaves, and buffer zones.

HRHB.headline: RS shifts to holding current gains
HRHB.body: Pale orders VRS formations to fortify existing positions and rebuild supply. HVO planners expect fewer new thrusts, but stronger prepared defenses.

RBiH.headline: Pale consolidates its holdings
RBiH.body: RS leadership favors digging in over costly advances. Sarajevo sees a defensive posture built around corridors, the Drina, and approaches to the capital.

HRHB.headline: Pale offers talks from a hard position
HRHB.body: RS leadership engages mediators while holding its military gains. HVO staff see Belgrade pressure easing if Pale can appear cooperative.

RBiH.headline: RS signals negotiation from strength
RBiH.body: Pale moves toward talks without giving up its map position. Sarajevo reads the posture as diplomatic pressure backed by current territorial control.

HRHB.headline: RS signals openness to partition terms
HRHB.body: Pale indicates willingness to accept a territorial settlement for recognition. HVO leaders see lower RS isolation, with a visible risk of hardline backlash.

RBiH.headline: Pale considers a partition framework
RBiH.body: RS leadership signals that a territorial settlement may be acceptable. Sarajevo sees potential diplomatic movement, but also a bid to legitimize wartime control.

title: Strategic Posture Review
narrative: Zagreb's expectations grow heavier with each passing month. The HVO holds territory across Herzegovina, but central Bosnia slips away and the war with the Bosniaks bleeds both sides white. Tudjman watches the map. Your assembly watches Tudjman. What direction will Herceg-Bosna take in the months ahead?

effect.text: The Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna reviews its strategic direction.

response_options.label: Press Bosnian Croat territorial objectives
response_options.description: Secure HVO holdings in Herzegovina and push for more. Morale rises among the faithful — but international pressure mounts and the Bosniak alliance, if it was ever real, is finished.

response_options.label: Coordinate with the Bosniaks
response_options.description: Seek tactical coordination with ARBiH against the VRS. Zagreb may be displeased, but the Washington Agreement's logic is sound: a unified front is more powerful than two wars at once.

response_options.label: Consolidate and resupply
response_options.description: Pause offensive operations, secure the supply corridor from Croatia, and build up reserves for the spring. What we hold, we hold. What we need, we will take when we are ready.

response_options.label: Accept the Federation framework
response_options.description: The war with the Bosniaks has cost Herceg-Bosna more than it can bear. The Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina offers a path to coexistence — and to Croatian recognition in Europe. Zagreb presses for it. The hardliners in Mostar will never forgive you.

RBiH.headline: Herceg-Bosna presses Croat objectives
RBiH.body: Mostar orders HVO leaders to secure current holdings and push for more. Sarajevo reads the posture as another strain on any remaining Bosniak-Croat coordination.

RS.headline: HVO posture turns more assertive
RS.body: Herceg-Bosna prioritizes Croat territorial objectives and accepts greater international pressure. Pale sees the Bosniak-Croat line weakening under competing aims.

RBiH.headline: Herceg-Bosna seeks tactical coordination
RBiH.body: Mostar signals renewed cooperation with ARBiH against the VRS. Sarajevo sees a stronger combined front, while Zagreb's reaction remains a constraint.

RS.headline: HVO and ARBiH coordination improves
RS.body: Herceg-Bosna moves toward tactical cooperation with Sarajevo. Pale planners see a more coherent anti-VRS alignment if the arrangement holds.

RBiH.headline: Herceg-Bosna pauses to resupply
RBiH.body: Mostar slows offensive operations to secure Croatian supply routes and rebuild cohesion. Sarajevo sees a steadier HVO posture, but not a political settlement.

RS.headline: HVO consolidates and rebuilds supply
RS.body: Herceg-Bosna focuses on holding territory and preparing reserves. Pale expects fewer immediate HVO attacks, with stronger logistics later.

RBiH.headline: Herceg-Bosna accepts the Federation path
RBiH.body: Mostar signals acceptance of a Federation framework with Sarajevo. RBiH leaders see a major alliance opening, despite hardline resistance inside Herceg-Bosna.

RS.headline: Herceg-Bosna turns toward Federation
RS.body: HVO leadership accepts a framework for coexistence with Sarajevo and closer Western standing. Pale sees the risk of a stronger unified front.

title: Visit to the Front
narrative: Your chief of staff suggests a presidential visit to the front. The troops have been fighting for months without seeing their president. A visit would lift spirits — but it also means time away from Sarajevo, exposure to risk, and a political signal about which theater you prioritize. The tunnels to the city are open. The road to Tuzla is guarded. General Dudakovic's men in Bihac have received no official visit since the war began. Where will you go?

effect.text: Arrangements are made for the presidential visit.

response_options.label: Visit the Sarajevo front
response_options.description: You travel through the Butmir tunnel into besieged Sarajevo. The troops of the 1st Corps see their president sharing their siege. The international press is watching.

response_options.label: Visit the eastern front — Tuzla and the corridor
response_options.description: You visit 2nd Corps in Tuzla and the corridor towns. The commanders brief you on the Drina situation. Your presence in the northeast sends a message about what you are willing to defend.

response_options.label: Visit the Bihac pocket — 5th Corps
response_options.description: You visit General Dudakovic's isolated command. His men have held the Bihac pocket without relief or recognition for months. The visit costs logistics resources — but the 5th Corps has earned a presidential handshake.

response_options.label: Stay in Sarajevo — too much to manage
response_options.description: The diplomatic calendar is full. The UN is negotiating. The army will understand. You remain at the Presidency and conduct the visit through your chief of staff.

response_options.label: Visit with international press
response_options.description: You invite foreign journalists to accompany you. The visit becomes a media event — less about command presence, more about demonstrating the human cost of the siege to the world.

HRHB.headline: RBiH leadership visits Sarajevo front
HRHB.body: The RBiH presidency enters Sarajevo and signals solidarity with 1st Corps under siege conditions. Mostar sees a morale and international-attention move centered on the capital.

RS.headline: RBiH leadership visits Sarajevo front
RS.body: The RBiH presidency appears with 1st Corps in Sarajevo. Pale sees a visible morale signal inside the besieged capital, with international press attention attached.

HRHB.headline: RBiH Leadership Tours Northeastern Front
HRHB.body: RBiH officials are directing attention to Tuzla and the corridor towns. The visit signals that Sarajevo is prioritizing cohesion and defense in the northeast.

RS.headline: RBiH Leadership Tours Northeastern Front
RS.body: RBiH officials are directing attention to Tuzla and the corridor towns. The visit signals a public commitment to hold the northeastern front.

HRHB.headline: RBiH President Remains In Sarajevo
HRHB.body: The RBiH presidency is staying in Sarajevo while staff officers handle front-line contact. The decision keeps diplomatic and command work centered in the capital.

RS.headline: RBiH President Remains In Sarajevo
RS.body: The RBiH presidency is staying in Sarajevo while staff officers handle front-line contact. The decision keeps political attention on capital-level command and diplomacy.

HRHB.headline: Sarajevo visits the Bihac pocket
HRHB.body: RBiH leadership directs attention to Dudakovic's isolated 5th Corps. Mostar sees a morale and cohesion signal to the western pocket, with logistics costs attached.

RS.headline: Sarajevo visits the Bihac pocket
RS.body: RBiH leadership gives official attention to the isolated 5th Corps. Pale sees Sarajevo trying to reinforce morale in Bihac despite the pocket's logistical strain.

HRHB.headline: Sarajevo turns front visit into press event
HRHB.body: RBiH brings foreign journalists into the visit and emphasizes the human cost of the siege. Mostar sees stronger international messaging, but less pure command presence.

RS.headline: Sarajevo brings foreign press to front visit
RS.body: RBiH converts the visit into an international media event about siege conditions. Pale sees Sarajevo trading command focus for diplomatic pressure.

title: Visit to the Front
narrative: Your generals suggest a presidential tour of the front. The VRS soldier is loyal — but loyalty is a currency spent by long campaigns and poor rations. Mladic visits corps. The president must also be seen. The Posavina corridor is under constant pressure. Sarajevo's siege is the world's most-watched front. The Drina Corps holds the east. Where will Republika Srpska's president be seen today?

response_options.label: Visit the Posavina corridor
response_options.description: You travel to the corridor — the lifeline connecting eastern and western Republika Srpska. The soldiers who hold this land know that everything depends on them.

response_options.label: Visit the Sarajevo siege lines — SRK positions
response_options.description: You visit the SRK positions overlooking the city. The symbolism is not lost on anyone — president and army, watching the capital of a state they do not recognize.

response_options.label: Visit the Drina Corps area
response_options.description: You travel east to the Drina Corps. General Zivanovic's men hold the eastern front — Zepa, Gorazde, the enclaves. Your presence there is noted internationally.

response_options.label: Stay in Pale — governance demands it
response_options.description: The Assembly is in session. International contacts require your attention. The front will see you another time. Your staff relays your greetings to the corps commanders.

response_options.label: Visit with international press
response_options.description: You invite foreign journalists to accompany you. The tour becomes a media opportunity — demonstrating confidence, normalcy, and RS authority over its territory.

HRHB.headline: RS Leadership Visits Posavina Corridor
HRHB.body: The RS presidency is emphasizing the Posavina corridor and the forces holding the northern link between RS territories.

RBiH.headline: RS Leadership Visits Posavina Corridor
RBiH.body: The RS presidency is emphasizing the Posavina corridor and the forces holding the northern link between RS territories.

HRHB.headline: RS leadership visits Sarajevo lines
HRHB.body: The RS presidency appears at SRK positions overlooking Sarajevo. Mostar sees a command-presence signal around the capital and a posture that raises international pressure.

RBiH.headline: RS leadership visits Sarajevo lines
RBiH.body: The RS presidency appears at positions overlooking Sarajevo. Sarajevo sees Pale reinforcing the siege-line posture while accepting greater international scrutiny.

HRHB.headline: RS leadership tours Drina Corps area
HRHB.body: The RS presidency turns public attention to the eastern front and Drina Corps positions. Mostar sees a morale signal to RS forces in the east, with international attention attached.

RBiH.headline: RS leadership tours Drina Corps area
RBiH.body: The RS presidency visits the eastern front and Drina Corps area. Sarajevo sees Pale signaling commitment around the enclaves while taking a further international-standing cost.

HRHB.headline: RS President Stays In Pale
HRHB.body: The RS presidency is keeping the front visit at staff level while the Assembly and outside contacts remain active in Pale.

RBiH.headline: RS President Stays In Pale
RBiH.body: The RS presidency is keeping the front visit at staff level while the Assembly and outside contacts remain active in Pale.

title: Visit to the Front
narrative: Your defence minister suggests a presidential tour of HVO positions. The Croatian fighters in Herzegovina have heard your words on the radio — they need to see your face. Central Bosnia is bleeding. Herzegovina holds. The Neretva front defines Herceg-Bosna's southern boundary. A visit is overdue. Where will the president of the Croatian Community be seen?

effect.text: The presidential tour of HVO positions is arranged.

response_options.label: Visit the Mostar front
response_options.description: You tour HVO positions around the city. East Mostar is under blockade and your soldiers hold the western bank. The international press watches every step you take here.

response_options.label: Visit central Bosnia — the embattled garrisons
response_options.description: You travel to the Vitez-Busovaca pocket, to Blaskic's battered command. The men holding central Bosnia fight with desperation and dwindling supplies. Your presence tells them they have not been abandoned.

response_options.label: Visit HVO positions on the Posavina front
response_options.description: You tour HVO positions in the north — Orasje, the Sava River line. These fighters hold the northernmost HVO territory, pressed between the VRS and the Sava. They need to know Mostar has not forgotten them.

response_options.label: Stay in Mostar — diplomatic contacts are urgent
response_options.description: The Zagreb line is active. The European monitors want a meeting. You remain in the capital and conduct the visit through your deputy commander. The front will understand.

response_options.label: Visit with international press
response_options.description: You invite European and American journalists. The tour is managed: show the HVO as defenders, show civilians on the Croatian side, avoid the detention camps. It is politics dressed as a front-line visit.

RBiH.headline: HRHB Leadership Visits Posavina Positions
RBiH.body: HRHB officials are touring HVO positions along the Sava line, signaling continued attention to the northern front.

RS.headline: HRHB Leadership Visits Posavina Positions
RS.body: HRHB officials are touring HVO positions along the Sava line, signaling continued attention to the northern front.

RBiH.headline: HRHB President Stays In Mostar
RBiH.body: HRHB leadership is keeping the front visit at deputy-command level while diplomatic contacts continue in Mostar.

RS.headline: HRHB President Stays In Mostar
RS.body: HRHB leadership is keeping the front visit at deputy-command level while diplomatic contacts continue in Mostar.

RBiH.headline: Herceg-Bosna tours the Mostar front
RBiH.body: HRHB leadership visits HVO positions around Mostar while international attention remains on the city. Sarajevo sees a morale signal to HVO troops, but also diplomatic exposure.

RS.headline: Herceg-Bosna tours the Mostar front
RS.body: HRHB leadership puts public attention on HVO positions around Mostar. Pale sees an HVO cohesion signal in Herzegovina, with international scrutiny attached.

RBiH.headline: Herceg-Bosna visits central Bosnia garrisons
RBiH.body: HRHB leadership travels to the Vitez-Busovaca pocket and signals that the central Bosnia garrisons have not been abandoned. Sarajevo sees morale support for an embattled HVO command.

RS.headline: Herceg-Bosna visits central Bosnia garrisons
RS.body: HRHB leadership gives attention to the Vitez-Busovaca pocket and its supply strain. Pale sees HVO cohesion reinforced in central Bosnia.
